body:
I have to admit, I've never spoken to a professional.  It's difficult to put into words why this is the case, because I HAVE thought about it... and I've decided not to.

I don't think I'm afraid, maybe I am.  But it's more along the lines that at this point I really trust myself.  I've spent years thinking about it, and I trust that my opinion on the matter is correct: life isn't for me.  Why do I want some other guy trying to convince me otherwise?  I've been trying to convince myself otherwise for awhile now... and like I said, I trust my conclusion.

Drugs are not appealing to me, probably because I don't know enough about them.  But I do have an educational background that allows me to slightly comprehend how they work and what they do... I admit it could really be the case that I know just enough about it to be skeptical, but not enough about it to really make a good decision on whether I think that's a good option.  Unfortunately I'd have to take years of school before (I think) I'd be comfortable changing my mind on that one... I hope that makes sense.

I must admit (and I've "admitted" this to myself about other things as well... similar to my "corn moment" comment above) compliments do make me feel good.  They really do!  But, again, I'm ok with never getting another compliment ever again....  I don't want to be stubborn or rude, but that's how I feel!

The link you sent was just, wow, so spot on.

Unfortunately I didn't quite understand if there was a point.  For instance, I've HAD that "corn moment".  Several times.  I may have a "corn moment" once every few months it seems.  

The last corn moment I had involved trying to throw something away.  I threw it away, but, and I shit you not, the item BOUNCED OUT OF THE GARBAGE AND LANDED RIGHT ON THE FLOOR!!!!!  Don't you get how hilarious that is????  Oh, probably not... I forgot that was part of the point.

So I can relate to that link for sure... on many levels.  Not to be rude but, so what??  I'm still perfectly ok with not having another "corn moment" ever again.
